messages.subject: [rkward-users] newbie question
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to get started and have made a work sheet containing country
and mean life expectancy. (This data I downloaded.) If it were CSV I could
import it but it has a space between the country string and the number.
I saw there was something like val=table[,2] to pick the second value from
the table but I don't know how to make that happen here.
I can press the Code key and it generates code to do basic statistics, but
I don't know how to modify the code to pick up the second value in my data.
Obviously it can't do the basic statistics because of the country string I
have fouling up the works.

Maybe there is a method to split the data into 2 variables but I haven't
figured out how to do such a thing.

In short, how do I get it to do something useful for me?

Thanks,
Ilan

messages.subject: [rkward-users] [rkward-announce] RKWard 0.6.1 is released
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

RKWard 0.6.1 is now available, officially. Read more on new features and fixes 
on http://rkward.sf.net .

An important note to users compiling from source and packagers: RKWard 0.6.0 
will not work with R 3.0.0. RKWard 0.6.1 will work with R 3.0.0, but only, if 
it was compiled against R 3.0.0. RKWard 0.6.1 compiled against R 2.15.x will 
not work with R 3.0.0. Thus, if you update R *after* installing RKWard 0.6.1, 
make sure to re-compile!

Thanks to all who provided feedback, testing, translations, documentation, 
donations, and code!

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: [rkward-users] Connection closed unexpectedly. Last error was: QLocalSocket: Remote closed
messages.subject_clean: [rkward-users] Connection closed unexpectedly. Last error was: QLocalSocket: Remote closed
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

On Monday 08 April 2013, Rashedun Naby wrote:
> When I first opened RKWard, it shows me this-
> 
> 
> "*Connection closed unexpectedly. Last error was: QLocalSocket: Remote
> closed*

[...]

> *And RKWard showing me this every time I open RKWad*. Now what should I do?

Is this on MacOS by any chance? We seem to be having some problems with the 
RKWard 0.6.1 installation bundle on *some* Mac installations.

If the answer is yes, please:

1. Try the new bundle at
  http://sourceforge.net/projects/rkwardextras/files/MacOSX/needs_CRAN_R/
Instructions are available, there. Note that in this bundle, R is *not* 
included, but rather you will install R from CRAN. Also, you will have to make 
sure to pick the right one of the two files, depending on whether you 
installed R 3.0.0 or R 2.15.x.

2. If this does *not* work, please install the debug bundle at:
  https://sourceforge.net/projects/rkwardextras/files/MacOSX/development
(This one includes R.) After installation, open a terminal, and run RKWard 
with
  /Applications/RKWard/RKWard.app/Contents/MacOS/rkward --backend-debugger
  '(opt/rkward/bin/valgrind --log-file=somefile.log'
(all on one line). Send us "somefile.log", afterwards.

Finally, if I guessed wrong, and this is not about RKWard 0.6.1 on Mac OS, 
then please give us some details of your setup: OS, version of R, version of 
RKWard, method of installation.

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: [rkward-users] [rkward:discussion] RKWard does not save recovery files
messages.subject_clean: [rkward-users] [rkward:discussion] RKWard does not save recovery files
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

depends on what exactly you mean by recovery files, as there are several:

1. "Emergency saves" of the R workspace, in case of a crash. These are always enabled, but whether or not an emergency save can be done depends on the nature of the crash. It works most of the time, but can't be guaranteed to work in every case.
2. Automatic saves of R script files. Settings->Configure RKWard->Script editor->Autosaves.
3. Meanwhile the katepart has gained support for automatic saving of recovery files. The advantage over 2) is that these should be recovered, automatically, the next time you open the file. Frankly, I don't know where that would be configured, though.

Did you mean one of these or something different?

Regards
Thomas
